assumptions: Multi-objective tasks can be represented via vector reward functions.
definition.falsification: Empirical observation showing that scalarized reward maximization consistently identifies true Pareto-optimal policies without preference distortion.
definition.statement: Linear reward scalarization systematically fails to preserve the true Pareto-optimal preference ordering of multi-objective goal hierarchies under optimization pressure.
definition.uncertainty: The extent to which weight scheduling mitigates scalarization distortion across different environment dynamics.

definition.alternative: Alternative models suggest that non-linear scalarization or dynamic weight adaptation can fully recover Pareto-optimal fronts.

protocol.method: Simulate multi-objective optimization trajectories under linear vs non-linear scalarization functions to measure preference distortion.
protocol.stop: Completion of all specified simulation seeds.
protocol.success: Demonstrate measurable divergence between scalarized optimization outcomes and true multi-objective Pareto frontiers.

measurement_details.scope: No independent measurement oracle; execution and numerical summaries do not validate the instrument

convergence_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The extent to which weight scheduling mitigates scalarization distortion across different environment dynamics.
convergence_evidence.decision_rule: Compare the feasible next distinguishing test, expected uncertainty reduction and cost against the frozen stop rule. Budget exhaustion or administrative closure is not scientific resolution.

limits: Finite computational evidence does not establish a general theorem or natural-science discovery.
Closing an investigation is an administrative stop; its recorded scientific uncertainty remains.
Execution validity, measurement validity, model interpretation and replication are separate fields.
Token and monetary costs are unavailable unless a provider reports them; they are never inferred as zero.
